L78: 
L79:     Abstract
L80: 
L81:        This document proposes an additional endpoint for OAuth authorization
L82:        servers, which allows clients to notify the authorization server that
L83:        a previously obtained refresh or access token is no longer needed.
L84:        This allows the authorization server to clean up security
L85:        credentials.  A revocation request will invalidate the actual token
L86:        and, if applicable, other tokens based on the same authorization
L87:        grant.
L88:

L75: ## 【23†Abstract】
L76: 
L77: This document describes a mechanism for sender-constraining OAuth 2.0 tokens via a proof-of-possession mechanism on the application level. This mechanism allows for the detection of replay attacks with access and refresh tokens.【24†¶】

L89: ## 【34†1.】 【35†Introduction】 【36†Skip to TOC】
L90: Demonstrating Proof of Possession (DPoP) is an application-level mechanism for sender-constraining OAuth [【37†RFC6749】] access and refresh tokens. It enables a client to prove the possession of a public/private key pair by including a `DPoP` header in an HTTP request. The value of the header is a JSON Web Token (JWT) [【38†RFC7519】] that enables the authorization server to bind issued tokens to the public part of a client's key pair.
L91: Recipients of such tokens are then able to verify the binding of the token to the key pair that the client has demonstrated that it holds via the `DPoP` header, thereby providing some assurance that the client presenting the token also possesses the private key. In other words, the legitimate presenter of the token is constrained to be the sender that holds and proves possession of the private part of the key pair.【39†¶】
L92: The mechanism specified herein can be used in cases where other methods of sender-constraining tokens that utilize elements of the underlying secure transport layer, such as [【40†RFC8705】] or [【41†TOKEN-BINDING】], are not available or desirable.
L93: For example, due to a sub-par user experience of TLS client authentication in user agents and a lack of support for HTTP token binding, neither mechanism can be used if an OAuth client is an application that is dynamically downloaded and executed in a web browser (sometimes referred to as a "single-page application").
L94: Additionally, applications that are installed and run directly on a user's device are well positioned to benefit from DPoP-bound tokens that guard against the misuse of tokens by a compromised or malicious resource. Such applications often have dedicated protected storage for cryptographic keys.【42†¶】
L95: DPoP can be used to sender-constrain access tokens regardless of the client authentication method employed, but DPoP itself is not used for client authentication. DPoP can also be used to sender-constrain refresh tokens issued to public clients (those without authentication credentials associated with the `client_id`).【43†¶】
